input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having trouble sending picture messages—those MMS things—from my phone. It’s been a few hours now and nothing seems to go through. Can you help me fix this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.

I just checked, and it looks like my phone shows "No Signal" at the top, and I think mobile data is turned off. I’m not sure about Wi-Fi, but I mainly use my phone for calls and texts, not really for browsing the web. What should I do next?

I checked again, and I still see "No Signal" at the top of my phone. I’m not sure how to tell if Airplane Mode is on or off—could you explain how to check that? Also, I’m a bit nervous about restarting my phone. Will I lose any of my photos or messages if I do that?

I checked the top of my screen, and I don’t see any airplane icon—just the "No Signal" message. So I guess Airplane Mode is off. What should I try next? I’m still a bit worried about restarting my phone, but if you’re sure it won’t delete anything, I can try it if you think it will help.
Okay, I restarted my phone like you said, but I still see "No Signal" at the top. It doesn’t look like anything changed. What should I do now? This is getting a bit frustrating.

Alright, I followed your instructions and took out the SIM card, then put it back in. Now I see bars at the top and something that says "5G," and it looks like mobile data is on again. Does this mean it’s working now? What should I do next?
I just tried to send a picture message, but it still won’t go through. It looks like I still can’t send MMS messages, even though I have signal now. What should I do next?

I checked my phone’s APN settings, and it says the APN name is "internet" and the MMSC URL is "http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc." I’m not sure if that’s right or not—does that look okay to you? What should I do next?
I went ahead and reset the APN settings like you suggested. Do I need to restart my phone again now? I just want to make sure I’m doing this right and won’t mess anything up.
I restarted my phone after resetting the APN settings, but I still can’t send picture messages. It’s still not working—what else can I try? This is getting a bit frustrating.
I checked, and my Wi-Fi is turned off, and Wi-Fi Calling is also off. So I don’t think that’s causing the problem. Is there anything else I should try?

I checked my messaging app’s permissions, and it looks like it only has permission for phone calls. It doesn’t seem to have access to storage or SMS. Could that be why I can’t send picture messages? How do I fix this?
I gave my messaging app permission for both storage and SMS, just like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else I can try? I’m starting to worry this will never work.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

I just checked, and it looks like my phone shows "No Signal" at the top, and I think mobile data is turned off. I’m not sure about Wi-Fi, but I mainly use my phone for calls and texts, not really for browsing the web. What should I do next?

Thank you for the update. Since your phone shows "No Signal" and mobile data is turned off, this means your device currently does not have cellular service, which is required for sending MMS messages.

Let’s start by troubleshooting your lack of signal. Please check the following on your phone:
1. Is Airplane Mode turned ON? If so, please turn it OFF.
2. If Airplane Mode is OFF, try restarting your phone to refresh the connection.
3. If you still see "No Signal," please check if your SIM card is properly inserted.

Can you confirm if Airplane Mode is off and, if so, try restarting your phone? Let me know what you see after these steps.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

I checked again, and I still see "No Signal" at the top of my phone. I’m not sure how to tell if Airplane Mode is on or off—could you explain how to check that? Also, I’m a bit nervous about restarting my phone. Will I lose any of my photos or messages if I do that?

No worries—restarting your phone will not delete any of your photos, messages, or other personal data. It simply turns your phone off and back on to refresh its connection to the network.

To check if Airplane Mode is on:
- Look for an airplane icon (✈️) at the top of your phone’s screen. If you see it, Airplane Mode is ON.
- If you don’t see the airplane icon, Airplane Mode is likely OFF.

If you do see the airplane icon, please turn Airplane Mode OFF by:
- Swiping down from the top of your screen to open the quick settings menu.
- Tapping the airplane icon to disable it.

Let me know if you see the airplane icon, and if turning it off changes your signal status. If Airplane Mode is already off and you’re still seeing "No Signal," please let me know, and we’ll continue troubleshooting.

Thank you for confirming that Airplane Mode is off. Restarting your phone is a safe step and will not delete any of your data—it simply refreshes your phone’s connection to the network and can often resolve signal issues.

Please go ahead and restart your phone:

- Select “Restart” (or “Reboot”).
- Wait for your phone to turn off and back on.
